_README: RXL/iRetail -> OASIS canonical schema profile. VERIFIED 2026-08-11 against a real RXL database (TESTING11, 999 tables) rather than against documentation. Usage: OASIS_VIEW_SCHEMA=OASIS OASIS_STORE_LEVEL=<your store tier> OASIS_SCHEMA_PROFILE=rxl_schema_profile.json OASIS_DB_DIALECT=mssql python entrypoint.py --mode build-views > rxl_views.sql ; a DBA runs rxl_views.sql, then sets the OASIS login's DEFAULT_SCHEMA to OASIS so the adapter's unqualified reads resolve to these views. The views are read-only and touch nothing in dbo.
_corrections: Earlier drafts of this file assumed ITEM_MST.DEPARTMENT / ACTIVE_FLAG / SCAN_ITM_CD / VENDOR_CD, VENDOR_ADDRESS_MST.VENDOR_CD / VENDOR_NAME, POS_SALES_DTL.NET_AMT / TOTAL_VALUE and a GRN_HDR table. NONE of those exist. Real names are below; GRN_HDR has no equivalent in this schema and is omitted (it is a RECOMMENDED table, so preflight WARNs rather than fails).

ITEM_MST.sql: SELECT i.ITM_CD AS ITM_CD, i.ITM_LONG_NAME AS ITM_LONG_NAME, i.ITM_NAME AS ITM_SHORT_NAME, i.ITM_CD AS SCAN_ITM_CD, i.ITM_CATEGORY_CD AS CATEGORY, COALESCE(d.DIV_DESC, i.ITM_DIV_CD) AS DEPARTMENT, CASE WHEN i.ITM_STATUS = 'O' THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END AS ACTIVE_FLAG, cp.BCP_VEND_CD AS SUPPLIER_CD, i.ITM_STOCK_UOM AS UOM_CD, i.ITM_STOCK_UOM AS UOM_DESC, 'N' AS WEIGHT_FLAG FROM dbo.ITEM_MST i LEFT JOIN dbo.DIVISION_MST d ON d.DIV_ID = i.ITM_DIV_CD OUTER APPLY (SELECT TOP 1 BCP_VEND_CD FROM dbo.BASIC_CP_MST c WHERE c.BCP_ITEM_CD = i.ITM_CD AND c.BCP_VEND_CD IS NOT NULL ORDER BY c.BCP_LAST_UPD_DATE DESC) cp
ITEM_MST._why_sql: SUPPLIER_CD is NOT on ITEM_MST in RXL — the item/vendor link is BASIC_CP_MST.BCP_VEND_CD, and an item can have several, so we take the most recently updated. DEPARTMENT is a code (ITM_DIV_CD) resolved to a name via DIVISION_MST. Neither can be expressed as a 1:1 column rename.
ITEM_MST._why_case: ACTIVE_FLAG is VALUE-normalised, not just renamed. RXL marks an active item ITM_STATUS='O' (open); the OASIS contract means 'Y'. Mapping the column straight through returned 39,728 rows that the adapter then filtered to ZERO on `WHERE ACTIVE_FLAG='Y'` — a silent empty result, not an error. Mapping a schema means mapping the VOCABULARY, not only the column names.

STOCK_MASTER.sql: SELECT s.SM_ITM_CD AS SM_ITM_CD, s.SM_ORG_CD AS SM_ORG_CD, s.SM_CURR_STK_QTY AS SM_QTY, s.SM_WT_AVG_COST AS SM_WAC, COALESCE(mv.LAST_RECV, i.ITM_LAST_PURCH_DT) AS SM_LAST_RECV_DT FROM dbo.STOCK_MASTER s LEFT JOIN dbo.ITEM_MST i ON i.ITM_CD = s.SM_ITM_CD OUTER APPLY (SELECT MAX(m.TXN_DATE) AS LAST_RECV FROM dbo.ITEM_MOVEMENT_DATE m WHERE m.ITM_CD = s.SM_ITM_CD AND m.ORG_CD = s.SM_ORG_CD AND m.RECEIVED_QTY > 0) mv WHERE s.SM_LEVEL_NUMBER = :store_level
STOCK_MASTER._why_sql: SM_LAST_RECV_DT drives days_since_delivery, which drives the DEAD-STOCK and STALE-FRESH guards. Mapping it to NULL (the earlier draft) set days_since_delivery=0 for every SKU, so `days_since_delivery > 200` was never true and BOTH guards were silently disabled — the engine then recommended ~6,800 never-sold, zero-stock lines. It fails OPEN: a disabled guard over-orders. RXL does carry the data, just not on STOCK_MASTER: ITEM_MOVEMENT_DATE is a per-store/per-item/per-day movement ledger (RECEIVED_QTY), with ITEM_MST.ITM_LAST_PURCH_DT as a per-item fallback.

SUPPLIER_MST._note: RXL carries none of lead time / reliability / order frequency. OASIS derives them from its own supplier patterns, NOT from the ERP.

ORGANIZATION_MST._note: RXL has no ACTIVE_FLAG on ORGANIZATION_MST; the level filter already selects live store rows.
